meta.topic: 级数：调和级数、交错级数与绝对/条件收敛、幂级数、泰勒级数、傅里叶级数、正项级数判别法

zh: 设 $H_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac1k$ 为第 $n$ 个部分和。因为 $H_{n+1}-H_n=\frac1{n+1}>0$，数列 $\{H_n\}$ 严格递增；由单调有界原理，$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1n$ 收敛当且仅当 $\{H_n\}$ 有上界。通项 $\frac1n\to0$ 只说明收敛的必要条件成立，不能由此断言收敛。

把下标按 $1,2,4,\dots$ 分组。对 $j=1,\dots,k$，第 $j$ 组为 $$\frac1{2^{j-1}+1}+\frac1{2^{j-1}+2}+\cdots+\frac1{2^j},$$ 共 $2^{j-1}$ 项，且每项不小于该组最后一项 $\frac1{2^j}$，故组和至少为 $2^{j-1}\cdot\frac1{2^j}=\frac12$。于是 $$\begin{aligned}H_{2^k}&=1+\sum_{j=1}^{k}\left(\frac1{2^{j-1}+1}+\cdots+\frac1{2^j}\right)\\&\ge 1+\frac{k}{2}.\end{aligned}$$
对任意 $M>0$，取整数 $k>2(M-1)$，则 $H_{2^k}\ge1+\frac k2>M$。因此部分和无上界；又 $\{H_n\}$ 单调递增，故 $H_n\to+\infty$，即调和级数发散。由于 $H_n-H_{N-1}=\sum_{k=N}^{n}\frac1k$ 同样无界，任何尾部也发散；删去或改动有限项不改变发散性。

用积分比较给出增长速度。对 $x\in[k,k+1]$ 有 $\frac1x\le\frac1k$，积分得 $\int_k^{k+1}\frac{dx}{x}\le\frac1k$，对 $k=1,\dots,n$ 求和得 $$\ln(n+1)=\int_1^{n+1}\frac{dx}{x}\le H_n.$$ 另一方面，对 $k\ge2$ 和 $x\in[k-1,k]$ 有 $\frac1x\ge\frac1k$，故 $\frac1k\le\int_{k-1}^{k}\frac{dx}{x}$，求和得 $H_n-1\le\ln n$。合并得 $$\ln(n+1)\le H_n\le1+\ln n.$$ 这再次证明 $H_n\to\infty$，并说明发散速度是对数级的；进一步可证 $H_n-\ln n$ 单调递减且有下界，故 $H_n=\ln n+\gamma+o(1)$，$\gamma\approx0.5772$。

作为对照，考虑 $p$ 级数 $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{n^p}$。当 $p>1$ 时，$f(x)=x^{-p}$ 在 $[1,+\infty)$ 上正、连续、递减，且 $$\begin{aligned}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\frac1{n^p}&\le1+\int_1^{N}\frac{dx}{x^p}\\&<1+\int_1^{+\infty}\frac{dx}{x^p}=1+\frac1{p-1}.\end{aligned}$$ 部分和有上界，故收敛。当 $0<p\le1$ 时 $\frac1{n^p}\ge\frac1n$，与调和级数比较得发散；当 $p\le0$ 时通项不趋于 $0$，更直接发散。因此 $p=1$ 恰是分界线：指数稍大于 $1$ 就收敛，而 $p=1$ 仍发散；这与「通项趋于 $0$」并不矛盾。
en: Let $H_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}\frac1k$ be the $n$-th partial sum. Since $H_{n+1}-H_n=\frac1{n+1}>0$, the sequence $\{H_n\}$ is strictly increasing; by the monotone convergence principle, $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1n$ converges if and only if $\{H_n\}$ is bounded above. The condition $\frac1n\to0$ only verifies the necessary condition for convergence and does not by itself prove convergence.

Group the indices as $1,2,4,\dots$ terms. For $j=1,\dots,k$, the $j$-th block is $$\frac1{2^{j-1}+1}+\frac1{2^{j-1}+2}+\cdots+\frac1{2^j},$$ which has $2^{j-1}$ terms, each at least the last term $\frac1{2^j}$; hence the block sum is at least $2^{j-1}\cdot\frac1{2^j}=\frac12$. Therefore $$\begin{aligned}H_{2^k}&=1+\sum_{j=1}^{k}\left(\frac1{2^{j-1}+1}+\cdots+\frac1{2^j}\right)\\&\ge 1+\frac{k}{2}.\end{aligned}$$

For any $M>0$, choose an integer $k>2(M-1)$; then $H_{2^k}\ge1+\frac k2>M$. Thus the partial sums are unbounded, and since $\{H_n\}$ is increasing, $H_n\to+\infty$: the harmonic series diverges. Because $H_n-H_{N-1}=\sum_{k=N}^{n}\frac1k$ is also unbounded, every tail diverges; deleting or changing finitely many terms does not affect divergence.

Integral comparison gives the growth rate. For $x\in[k,k+1]$, $\frac1x\le\frac1k$, so $\int_k^{k+1}\frac{dx}{x}\le\frac1k$; summing over $k=1,\dots,n$ yields $$\ln(n+1)=\int_1^{n+1}\frac{dx}{x}\le H_n.$$ Conversely, for $k\ge2$ and $x\in[k-1,k]$, $\frac1x\ge\frac1k$, so $\frac1k\le\int_{k-1}^{k}\frac{dx}{x}$; summing gives $H_n-1\le\ln n$. Combining, $$\ln(n+1)\le H_n\le1+\ln n.$$ This reproves $H_n\to\infty$ and shows logarithmic growth; moreover $H_n-\ln n$ is decreasing and bounded below, so $H_n=\ln n+\gamma+o(1)$ with $\gamma\approx0.5772$.

For comparison, consider the $p$-series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{n^p}$. For $p>1$, the function $f(x)=x^{-p}$ is positive, continuous and decreasing on $[1,+\infty)$, and $$\begin{aligned}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\frac1{n^p}&\le1+\int_1^{N}\frac{dx}{x^p}\\&<1+\int_1^{+\infty}\frac{dx}{x^p}=1+\frac1{p-1}.\end{aligned}$$ so the partial sums are bounded and the series converges. For $0<p\le1$, $\frac1{n^p}\ge\frac1n$, so comparison with the harmonic series gives divergence; for $p\le0$ the terms do not tend to $0$, so divergence is immediate. Hence $p=1$ is exactly the borderline: raising the exponent slightly above $1$ gives convergence, while $p=1$ still diverges; this is consistent with the fact that the terms tend to $0$.

zh: 由第 1 步，$S$ 夹在相邻部分和之间：$n$ 为偶数时 $S_n\le S\le S_{n+1}$，$n$ 为奇数时 $S_{n+1}\le S\le S_n$。因此 $$|R_n|=|S-S_n|\le|S_{n+1}-S_n|=u_{n+1}.$$ 这就是莱布尼茨余项估计：用前 $n$ 项近似和，误差不超过被舍弃的第一项。注意它只给出上界，并不表示误差恰好等于 $u_{n+1}$。

若 $\sum|u_n|$ 收敛，则称 $\sum u_n$ 绝对收敛。此时对任意 $\varepsilon>0$，由 $\sum|u_n|$ 的柯西准则存在 $N$，使 $n>m\ge N$ 时 $\sum_{k=m+1}^{n}|u_k|<\varepsilon$。由三角不等式 $$\left|\sum_{k=m+1}^{n}u_k\right|\le\sum_{k=m+1}^{n}|u_k|<\varepsilon,$$ 所以 $\sum u_n$ 的部分和是柯西列，因而收敛，并且 $\left|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}u_n\right|\le\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|u_n|$。这说明绝对收敛蕴含收敛。

若 $\sum u_n$ 收敛而 $\sum|u_n|$ 发散，则称 $\sum u_n$ 条件收敛。典型例子是交错调和级数：$u_n=\frac1n$ 单调递减趋于 $0$，由莱布尼茨判别法 $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}$ 收敛；但绝对值级数是调和级数，发散，所以它条件收敛。其和可这样求出：对 $t\ne-1$ 有 $$\frac1{1+t}=\sum_{k=0}^{n}(-t)^k+\frac{(-t)^{n+1}}{1+t},$$ 在 $[0,1]$ 上积分，余项绝对值不超过 $\int_0^1t^{n+1}\,dt=\frac1{n+2}\to0$，故 $\ln2=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}$。

绝对收敛与条件收敛的差别在运算中很实际。若 $\sum u_n$ 绝对收敛，则任意重排、合并或拆项都不改变和；若只条件收敛，黎曼重排定理说：可以重排使新级数收敛到任意指定的实数，也可以使它发散。粗略理由是，条件收敛时正项部分与负项部分都发散（否则级数会绝对收敛或发散），于是可以先用正项累加超过目标值，再用负项拉回，周而复始；通项趋于 $0$ 保证每次调整的幅度越来越小。因此对条件收敛级数不能随意交换求和次序。

莱布尼茨判别法中的单调性条件不能去掉。取 $$u_n=\begin{cases}\frac1n,&n\ \text{为奇数},\\\frac1{n^2},&n\ \text{为偶数}.\end{cases}$$ 则 $u_n>0$ 且 $u_n\to0$，但 $u_{2k}=\frac1{4k^2}<\frac1{2k+1}=u_{2k+1}$，故 $\{u_n\}$ 不单调递减。对应的交错级数中，奇数项为正的 $\frac1{2k-1}$，其和发散；偶数项为负的 $-\frac1{(2k)^2}$，其和收敛。因此正项部分使部分和趋于 $+\infty$，整个级数发散。可见仅有 $u_n\to0$ 不足以保证交错级数收敛。
en: Let $u_n>0$, $u_n\ge u_{n+1}$, and $u_n\to0$, and consider $S_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}(-1)^{k-1}u_k$. The even partial sums $$S_{2m}=(u_1-u_2)+(u_3-u_4)+\cdots+(u_{2m-1}-u_{2m})$$ have nonnegative brackets, so $\{S_{2m}\}$ is increasing; on the other hand $$S_{2m}=u_1-[(u_2-u_3)+\cdots+(u_{2m-2}-u_{2m-1})]-u_{2m}\le u_1,$$ so it is bounded above; the odd partial sums $$S_{2m+1}=u_1-(u_2-u_3)-\cdots-(u_{2m}-u_{2m+1})$$ are decreasing and $S_{2m+1}\ge S_2$. Hence $S_{2m}\to S$; since $S_{2m+1}=S_{2m}+u_{2m+1}$ and $u_{2m+1}\to0$, also $S_{2m+1}\to S$. Therefore $S_n\to S$ and the alternating series converges.

By Step 1, $S$ lies between consecutive partial sums: if $n$ is even, $S_n\le S\le S_{n+1}$; if $n$ is odd, $S_{n+1}\le S\le S_n$. Hence $$|R_n|=|S-S_n|\le|S_{n+1}-S_n|=u_{n+1}.$$ This is the Leibniz remainder estimate: using the first $n$ terms, the error is at most the first omitted term. It gives only an upper bound, not the exact error.

If $\sum|u_n|$ converges, then $\sum u_n$ is called absolutely convergent. For any $\varepsilon>0$, the Cauchy criterion for $\sum|u_n|$ gives $N$ such that $n>m\ge N$ implies $\sum_{k=m+1}^{n}|u_k|<\varepsilon$. By the triangle inequality, $$\left|\sum_{k=m+1}^{n}u_k\right|\le\sum_{k=m+1}^{n}|u_k|<\varepsilon,$$ so the partial sums of $\sum u_n$ form a Cauchy sequence and converge; moreover $\left|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}u_n\right|\le\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}|u_n|$. Thus absolute convergence implies convergence.

If $\sum u_n$ converges but $\sum|u_n|$ diverges, then $\sum u_n$ is conditionally convergent. The standard example is the alternating harmonic series: $u_n=\frac1n$ decreases monotonically to $0$, so $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}$ converges by the Leibniz test; its absolute-value series is the divergent harmonic series, so convergence is conditional. Its sum is found as follows: for $t\ne-1$, $$\frac1{1+t}=\sum_{k=0}^{n}(-t)^k+\frac{(-t)^{n+1}}{1+t}.$$ Integrating over $[0,1]$, the remainder is at most $\int_0^1t^{n+1}\,dt=\frac1{n+2}\to0$, hence $\ln2=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}$.

The difference between absolute and conditional convergence matters in operations. If $\sum u_n$ is absolutely convergent, arbitrary rearrangements, groupings and splittings leave the sum unchanged; if it is only conditionally convergent, Riemann's rearrangement theorem says that a rearrangement can converge to any prescribed real number, or can be made to diverge. Roughly, conditional convergence forces both the positive part and the negative part to diverge (otherwise the series would be absolutely convergent or divergent), so one can add positive terms until the sum exceeds a target, then negative terms until it falls below, and repeat; the terms tending to $0$ make the adjustments smaller and smaller. Hence a conditionally convergent series cannot be reordered freely.

The monotonicity hypothesis in the Leibniz test cannot be dropped. Take $$u_n=\begin{cases}\frac1n,&n\ \text{odd},\\\frac1{n^2},&n\ \text{even}.\end{cases}$$ Then $u_n>0$ and $u_n\to0$, but $u_{2k}=\frac1{4k^2}<\frac1{2k+1}=u_{2k+1}$, so $\{u_n\}$ is not decreasing. In the corresponding alternating series the positive odd terms are $\frac1{2k-1}$, whose sum diverges, while the negative even terms are $-\frac1{(2k)^2}$, whose sum converges. The positive part therefore drives the partial sums to $+\infty$, and the series diverges. Thus $u_n\to0$ alone does not guarantee convergence of an alternating series.

zh: 设幂级数 $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_n(x-x_0)^n$。固定 $x$ 后考察绝对值级数 $\sum|a_n||x-x_0|^n$。令 $$\rho=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{|a_n|}\in[0,+\infty],\qquad R=\frac1\rho,$$ 并约定 $\rho=0$ 时 $R=+\infty$，$\rho=+\infty$ 时 $R=0$。由根值判别法，$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{|a_n||x-x_0|^n}=\rho|x-x_0|$：当 $|x-x_0|<R$ 时该值小于 $1$，级数绝对收敛；当 $|x-x_0|>R$ 时该值大于 $1$，通项不趋于 $0$，级数发散。这正是柯西-阿达马公式，也是收敛半径存在的证明。

当系数满足 $a_n\ne0$（至少从某项起）且极限 $L=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right|$ 存在（或为 $+\infty$）时，对固定的 $x$， $$\begin{aligned}\left|\frac{a_{n+1}(x-x_0)^{n+1}}{a_n(x-x_0)^n}\right|&=\left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right||x-x_0|\\&\longrightarrow L|x-x_0|.\end{aligned}$$ 由比值判别法，$L|x-x_0|<1$ 时绝对收敛，$L|x-x_0|>1$ 时发散，故 $$R=\frac1L=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{a_n}{a_{n+1}}\right|,$$ 并约定 $L=0$ 时 $R=+\infty$，$L=+\infty$ 时 $R=0$。若该极限不存在，则不能使用此式，应回到柯西-阿达马公式。

在端点 $x=x_0\pm R$ 处，根值判别法的极限等于 $1$，必须把端点代回原级数单独判断；收敛域可能是开区间、闭区间或半开半闭区间。例如： $$\begin{aligned}&\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}x^n\ (R=1),\\&\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n}\ (R=1),\\&\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n^2}\ (R=1).\end{aligned}$$ 第一个在 $x=\pm1$ 处通项都不趋于 $0$，端点全发散，收敛域为 $(-1,1)$；第二个在 $x=1$ 是调和级数（发散），在 $x=-1$ 是交错调和级数（收敛），收敛域为 $[-1,1)$；第三个在 $x=\pm1$ 都绝对收敛（$\sum1/n^2$），收敛域为 $[-1,1]$。因此「先求 $R$，再验端点」是固定流程。

在收敛区间内部，幂级数具有很好的整体性质。任取 $0\le r<R$，当 $|x-x_0|\le r$ 时 $$|a_n(x-x_0)^n|\le|a_n|r^n,$$ 而 $\sum|a_n|r^n$ 在 $r<R$ 处收敛，故由魏尔斯特拉斯 $M$ 判别法，$\sum a_n(x-x_0)^n$ 在 $[x_0-r,x_0+r]$ 上一致收敛。每个部分和是连续函数，一致收敛保持连续性，所以和函数 $S(x)$ 在 $|x-x_0|<R$ 内连续。注意这是一致收敛于任意闭子区间，而不是在整个 $(-R,R)$ 上一致收敛。

逐项求导与逐项积分不改变收敛半径。求导级数 $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}na_n(x-x_0)^{n-1}$ 的系数满足 $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{n|a_n|}=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{|a_n|},$$ 因为 $n^{1/n}\to1$，故其收敛半径仍为 $R$；积分级数 $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{a_n}{n+1}(x-x_0)^{n+1}$ 的系数同理也给出相同半径。由第 4 步，求导级数在任意闭子区间 $[x_0-r,x_0+r]$（$r<R$）上也一致收敛，且原级数在 $x_0$ 处收敛，故可逐项求导；积分则只需原级数一致收敛。于是对 $|x-x_0|<R$， $$\begin{aligned}S'(x)&=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}na_n(x-x_0)^{n-1},\\ \int_{x_0}^{x}S(t)\,dt&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{a_n}{n+1}(x-x_0)^{n+1}.\end{aligned}$$ 但端点处的敛散性可能改变，必须重新检验。

以几何级数为例：$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}x^n=\frac1{1-x}$（$|x|<1$），由比值公式得 $R=1$，端点 $x=\pm1$ 处通项不趋于 $0$，故收敛域为 $(-1,1)$。在区间内逐项求导得 $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}nx^{n-1}=\frac1{(1-x)^2}\quad(|x|<1),$$ 逐项积分得 $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n}=-\ln(1-x)\quad(|x|<1).$$ 积分后的级数在 $x=-1$ 收敛（交错调和级数），由阿贝尔定理，和函数在 $x=-1$ 处单侧连续，取 $x\to-1^+$ 得 $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n}{n}=-\ln2$，即 $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}=\ln2$；而在 $x=1$ 处是调和级数，发散。这清楚显示：求导、积分保持 $R$ 不变，但端点必须重新判断。
en: Consider the power series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}a_n(x-x_0)^n$. For fixed $x$, examine the absolute series $\sum|a_n||x-x_0|^n$. Put $$\rho=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{|a_n|}\in[0,+\infty],\qquad R=\frac1\rho,$$ with the conventions $R=+\infty$ when $\rho=0$ and $R=0$ when $\rho=+\infty$. The root test gives $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{|a_n||x-x_0|^n}=\rho|x-x_0|$: if $|x-x_0|<R$ this is less than $1$ and the series converges absolutely; if $|x-x_0|>R$ it is greater than $1$, the terms do not tend to $0$, and the series diverges. This is the Cauchy–Hadamard formula and proves that a radius of convergence exists.

When $a_n\ne0$ eventually and the limit $L=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right|$ exists (possibly $+\infty$), then for fixed $x$, $$\begin{aligned}\left|\frac{a_{n+1}(x-x_0)^{n+1}}{a_n(x-x_0)^n}\right|&=\left|\frac{a_{n+1}}{a_n}\right||x-x_0|\\&\longrightarrow L|x-x_0|.\end{aligned}$$ By the ratio test, the series converges absolutely if $L|x-x_0|<1$ and diverges if $L|x-x_0|>1$; hence $$R=\frac1L=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{a_n}{a_{n+1}}\right|,$$ with $R=+\infty$ for $L=0$ and $R=0$ for $L=+\infty$. If the limit does not exist, this formula cannot be used; one must return to Cauchy–Hadamard.

At the endpoints $x=x_0\pm R$ the root test gives the limit $1$, so each endpoint must be substituted into the original series and examined separately; the interval of convergence may be open, closed, or half-open. For example: $$\begin{aligned}&\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}x^n\ (R=1),\\&\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n}\ (R=1),\\&\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n^2}\ (R=1).\end{aligned}$$ For the first, the terms at $x=\pm1$ do not tend to $0$, so both endpoints diverge and the interval is $(-1,1)$. For the second, $x=1$ gives the divergent harmonic series while $x=-1$ gives the convergent alternating harmonic series, so the interval is $[-1,1)$. For the third, both endpoints converge absolutely (as $\sum1/n^2$), so the interval is $[-1,1]$. Thus the fixed procedure is: find $R$ first, then test the endpoints.

Inside the interval a power series has strong global properties. Take any $0\le r<R$. For $|x-x_0|\le r$, $$|a_n(x-x_0)^n|\le|a_n|r^n,$$ and $\sum|a_n|r^n$ converges because $r<R$; by the Weierstrass $M$-test, $\sum a_n(x-x_0)^n$ converges uniformly on $[x_0-r,x_0+r]$. Each partial sum is continuous, and uniform convergence preserves continuity, so the sum $S(x)$ is continuous on $|x-x_0|<R$. Note that this is uniform convergence on every closed subinterval, not uniform convergence on the whole interval $(-R,R)$.

Term-by-term differentiation and integration preserve the radius of convergence. The coefficients of the differentiated series $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}na_n(x-x_0)^{n-1}$ satisfy $$\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{n|a_n|}=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{|a_n|},$$ since $n^{1/n}\to1$, so its radius is still $R$; the integrated series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{a_n}{n+1}(x-x_0)^{n+1}$ likewise has the same radius. By Step 4, the differentiated series also converges uniformly on every closed subinterval $[x_0-r,x_0+r]$ with $r<R$, and the original series converges at $x_0$; hence termwise differentiation is legitimate. Integration requires only uniform convergence of the original series. Thus, for $|x-x_0|<R$, $$\begin{aligned}S'(x)&=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}na_n(x-x_0)^{n-1},\\ \int_{x_0}^{x}S(t)\,dt&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{a_n}{n+1}(x-x_0)^{n+1}.\end{aligned}$$ The endpoint behaviour, however, may change and must be checked again.

Take the geometric series: $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}x^n=\frac1{1-x}$ for $|x|<1$. The ratio formula gives $R=1$, and at $x=\pm1$ the terms do not tend to $0$, so the interval of convergence is $(-1,1)$. Differentiating term by term inside the interval gives $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}nx^{n-1}=\frac1{(1-x)^2}\quad(|x|<1),$$ and integrating term by term gives $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n}=-\ln(1-x)\quad(|x|<1).$$ The integrated series converges at $x=-1$ (alternating harmonic series); by Abel's theorem the sum is one-sided continuous there, so letting $x\to-1^+$ gives $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^n}{n}=-\ln2$, i.e. $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}=\ln2$. At $x=1$ the series is the divergent harmonic series. This shows clearly that differentiation and integration keep $R$ fixed, but endpoints must be re-examined.

zh: 设 $f$ 在含 $x_0,x$ 的区间上有 $n+1$ 阶导数。泰勒公式给出 $$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=T_n(x)+R_n(x),\\ T_n(x)&=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\frac{f^{(k)}(x_0)}{k!}(x-x_0)^k,\end{aligned}$$ 其中拉格朗日余项为 $$R_n(x)=\frac{f^{(n+1)}(\xi)}{(n+1)!}(x-x_0)^{n+1},$$ $\xi$ 介于 $x_0$ 与 $x$ 之间。由系数 $\frac{f^{(n)}(x_0)}{n!}$ 形式地构成的幂级数 $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{f^{(n)}(x_0)}{n!}(x-x_0)^n$ 称为 $f$ 在 $x_0$ 处的泰勒级数；它是否收敛、收敛后是否等于 $f$，需另行讨论。若 $f$ 能写成幂级数，逐次求导并令 $x=x_0$ 可得系数唯一为 $\frac{f^{(n)}(x_0)}{n!}$。

关键判据：在泰勒级数收敛的 $x$ 处， $$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{f^{(n)}(x_0)}{n!}(x-x_0)^n\\&\iff\lim_{n\to\infty}R_n(x)=0.\end{aligned}$$ 理由是由泰勒公式 $f(x)-T_n(x)=R_n(x)$，而级数的部分和正是 $T_n(x)$。因此仅有「泰勒级数收敛」还不够：它的和可能不是 $f(x)$。必须直接估计 $R_n(x)$，或用幂级数唯一性等定理证明级数的和就是 $f$。

对 $f(x)=e^x$，$f^{(n)}(x)=e^x$，故 $f^{(n)}(0)=1$，麦克劳林级数为 $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n!}$。由比值公式 $$R=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{a_n}{a_{n+1}}\right|=\lim_{n\to\infty}(n+1)=+\infty.$$ 对固定 $x$，拉格朗日余项满足 $|R_n(x)|=\frac{e^{\xi}}{(n+1)!}|x|^{n+1}\le e^{|x|}\frac{|x|^{n+1}}{(n+1)!}\to0$（$\xi$ 介于 $0$ 与 $x$ 之间）。所以对每个实数 $x$ 都有 $e^x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n!}$。

对 $f(x)=\sin x$，各阶导数只取 $\pm\sin x,\pm\cos x$，故 $|f^{(k)}(x)|\le1$，从而 $$|R_n(x)|\le\frac{|x|^{n+1}}{(n+1)!}\to0\quad(\forall x\in\mathbb R).$$ 因此 $\sin x$ 的麦克劳林级数对一切实数收敛于 $\sin x$。在 $0$ 处求导得 $\sin^{(k)}(0)$ 依次为 $0,1,0,-1,\dots$，故 $$\begin{aligned}\sin x&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^nx^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!},\\ \cos x&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^nx^{2n}}{(2n)!}.\end{aligned}$$ 余弦的论证相同，因为 $\cos x=\sin'x$，也可直接对导数重复上述估计。

对 $f(x)=\ln(1+x)$，由比值公式得收敛半径 $R=1$：$a_n=\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}$，$|a_n/a_{n+1}|=(n+1)/n\to1$。在 $|x|<1$ 内，用几何和 $$\frac1{1+t}=\sum_{k=0}^{n}(-t)^k+\frac{(-t)^{n+1}}{1+t}$$ 从 $0$ 到 $x$ 积分（$x>-1$），余项满足 $$\left|\int_0^x\frac{(-t)^{n+1}}{1+t}\,dt\right|\le\begin{cases}\dfrac{|x|^{n+2}}{n+2},&x\ge0,\\[4pt] \dfrac{|x|^{n+2}}{(n+2)(1+x)},&-1<x<0,\end{cases}\to0,$$ 故 $\ln(1+x)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}x^n}{n}$（$-1<x<1$）。在 $x=1$ 处，余项不超过 $\frac1{n+2}\to0$，级数收敛于 $\ln2$；在 $x=-1$ 处级数为 $-\sum\frac1n$，发散。所以成立区间是 $(-1,1]$，端点必须分别判断。

反例说明「级数收敛」不等于「等于函数」。令 $$f(x)= egin{cases}e^{-1/x^2},&x
e0,\0,&x=0.\end{cases}$$ 对 $x
e0$，可用归纳法证明 $f^{(n)}(x)=P_n(1/x)e^{-1/x^2}$，其中 $P_n$ 是多项式；又对任意 $m$，$t^me^{-t}	o0$（$t	o+\infty$），由于 $P_n(1/x)$ 是多项式，取足够大的 $m$（依赖于 $P_n$ 的次数）便由 $t^me^{-t}	o0$ 得 $f^{(n)}(x)=o(x)$。于是 $$f^{(n)}(0)=\lim_{x	o0} rac{f^{(n-1)}(x)-f^{(n-1)}(0)}{x}=0,$$ 所有阶导数在 $0$ 处都为 $0$，麦克劳林级数恒等于 $0$，收敛半径为 $+\infty$。但 $f(x)>0$（$x
e0$），所以级数只在 $x=0$ 处等于 $f$。这里 $R_n(x)=f(x)
ot	o0$（$x
e0$），正好违反第 2 步的判据。因此泰勒级数收敛只是必要条件，余项趋于 $0$ 才是等式成立的关键。
en: Let $f$ have $n+1$ derivatives on an interval containing $x_0$ and $x$. Taylor's formula states $$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=T_n(x)+R_n(x),\\ T_n(x)&=\sum_{k=0}^{n}\frac{f^{(k)}(x_0)}{k!}(x-x_0)^k,\end{aligned}$$ with the Lagrange remainder $$R_n(x)=\frac{f^{(n+1)}(\xi)}{(n+1)!}(x-x_0)^{n+1},$$ where $\xi$ lies between $x_0$ and $x$. The formal power series $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{f^{(n)}(x_0)}{n!}(x-x_0)^n$ is called the Taylor series of $f$ at $x_0$; whether it converges, and whether it equals $f$, are separate questions. If $f$ can be represented by a power series, differentiating repeatedly and setting $x=x_0$ shows that the coefficients are uniquely $\frac{f^{(n)}(x_0)}{n!}$.

The key criterion: at any $x$ where the Taylor series converges, $$\begin{aligned}f(x)&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{f^{(n)}(x_0)}{n!}(x-x_0)^n\\&\iff\lim_{n\to\infty}R_n(x)=0.\end{aligned}$$ Indeed, Taylor's formula gives $f(x)-T_n(x)=R_n(x)$, and the partial sums of the series are exactly $T_n(x)$. Thus convergence of the Taylor series alone is not enough: its sum may differ from $f(x)$. One must either estimate $R_n(x)$ directly or use uniqueness of power-series representations to show that the sum is $f$.

For $f(x)=e^x$, $f^{(n)}(x)=e^x$, so $f^{(n)}(0)=1$ and the Maclaurin series is $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n!}$. The ratio formula gives $$R=\lim_{n\to\infty}\left|\frac{a_n}{a_{n+1}}\right|=\lim_{n\to\infty}(n+1)=+\infty.$$ For fixed $x$, the Lagrange remainder satisfies $|R_n(x)|=\frac{e^{\xi}}{(n+1)!}|x|^{n+1}\le e^{|x|}\frac{|x|^{n+1}}{(n+1)!}\to0$ with $\xi$ between $0$ and $x$. Hence $e^x=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{x^n}{n!}$ for every real $x$.

For $f(x)=\sin x$, every derivative is one of $\pm\sin x,\pm\cos x$, so $|f^{(k)}(x)|\le1$ and therefore $$|R_n(x)|\le\frac{|x|^{n+1}}{(n+1)!}\to0\quad(\forall x\in\mathbb R).$$ Thus the Maclaurin series of $\sin x$ converges to $\sin x$ for all real $x$. The derivatives at $0$ are $0,1,0,-1,\dots$, so $$\begin{aligned}\sin x&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^nx^{2n+1}}{(2n+1)!},\\ \cos x&=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^nx^{2n}}{(2n)!}.\end{aligned}$$ The argument for cosine is the same, since $\cos x=\sin'x$, or one repeats the derivative estimate directly.

For $f(x)=\ln(1+x)$, the ratio formula gives radius $R=1$: $a_n=\frac{(-1)^{n-1}}{n}$ and $|a_n/a_{n+1}|=(n+1)/n\to1$. For $|x|<1$, use the finite geometric identity $$\frac1{1+t}=\sum_{k=0}^{n}(-t)^k+\frac{(-t)^{n+1}}{1+t}$$ and integrate from $0$ to $x$ (with $x>-1$); the remainder satisfies $$\left|\int_0^x\frac{(-t)^{n+1}}{1+t}\,dt\right|\le\begin{cases}\dfrac{|x|^{n+2}}{n+2},&x\ge0,\\[4pt] \dfrac{|x|^{n+2}}{(n+2)(1+x)},&-1<x<0,\end{cases}\to0.$$ Hence $\ln(1+x)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n-1}x^n}{n}$ for $-1<x<1$. At $x=1$ the remainder is at most $\frac1{n+2}\to0$, so the series converges to $\ln2$; at $x=-1$ it becomes $-\sum\frac1n$, which diverges. The interval of validity is therefore $(-1,1]$, with the endpoints decided separately.

A counterexample shows that convergence of the series is not the same as equality with the function. Define $$f(x)= egin{cases}e^{-1/x^2},&x
e0,\0,&x=0.\end{cases}$$ For $x
e0$, induction shows $f^{(n)}(x)=P_n(1/x)e^{-1/x^2}$ for some polynomial $P_n$; and for every $m$, $t^me^{-t}	o0$ as $t	o+\infty$, Since $P_n(1/x)$ is a polynomial, taking $m$ sufficiently large (depending on the degree of $P_n$) gives $f^{(n)}(x)=o(x)$ from $t^me^{-t}	o0$. Therefore $$f^{(n)}(0)=\lim_{x	o0} rac{f^{(n-1)}(x)-f^{(n-1)}(0)}{x}=0,$$ so every derivative vanishes at $0$, the Maclaurin series is identically $0$, and its radius is $+\infty$. But $f(x)>0$ for $x
e0$, so the series equals $f$ only at $x=0$. Here $R_n(x)=f(x)
ot	o0$ for $x
e0$, exactly violating the criterion of Step 2. Thus convergence of the Taylor series is only necessary; the remainder tending to $0$ is what makes the equality hold.

zh: 设 $f$ 以 $2\pi$ 为周期，且在 $[-\pi,\pi]$ 上可积。三角函数系 $$1,\ \cos x,\ \sin x,\ \cos2x,\ \sin2x,\ \dots$$ 具有正交性：对 $n,m\ge1$， $$\begin{aligned}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\cos nx\cos mx\,dx&=\pi\delta_{nm},\\ \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\sin nx\sin mx\,dx&=\pi\delta_{nm},\end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\cos nx\sin mx\,dx&=0,\\ \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\cos nx\,dx&=\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\sin nx\,dx=0.\end{aligned}$$ 这些等式可由积化和差公式直接验证。正交性是后面「筛出」各频率系数的根本原因。

设 $f$ 能展开为一致收敛的三角级数 $$f(x)=\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(a_n\cos nx+b_n\sin nx).$$ 两边乘以 $\cos kx$（$k\ge1$）并在 $[-\pi,\pi]$ 上积分；由一致收敛可逐项积分，正交性使除 $a_k\cos kx$ 外各项积分为 $0$，得 $$\begin{aligned}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\cos kx\,dx&=a_k\pi,\\ a_k&=\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\cos kx\,dx.\end{aligned}$$ 乘以 $\sin kx$ 同理得 $b_k$。对 $k=0$，$\int f=\frac{a_0}{2}\cdot2\pi=\pi a_0$，故 $a_0=\frac1\pi\int f$；常数项写成 $\frac{a_0}{2}$ 正是为了让 $a_0$ 的公式与其余 $a_k$ 统一。

收敛性由狄利克雷定理保证：若 $f$ 以 $2\pi$ 为周期，在 $[-\pi,\pi]$ 上有界且分段单调（或分段光滑），并且只有有限个间断点，则其傅里叶级数在每一点收敛，且 $$S(x)=\frac{f(x^-)+f(x^+)}{2},$$ 其中 $f(x^\pm)$ 为单侧极限；在连续点 $S(x)=f(x)$，在跳跃点取左右极限的平均值。端点 $x=\pm\pi$ 处取 $\frac{f(-\pi^+)+f(\pi^-)}{2}$。注意「连续」本身不足以保证傅里叶级数收敛（存在连续函数的傅里叶级数在某点发散），所以分段单调或分段光滑的条件不能省略。

计算方波：设 $f(x)=-1$（$-\pi<x<0$），$f(x)=1$（$0<x<\pi$），并以 $2\pi$ 为周期。$f$ 是奇函数，故 $a_0=a_n=0$。对 $n\ge1$， $$\begin{aligned}b_n&=\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\sin nx\,dx\\&=\frac2\pi\int_0^{\pi}\sin nx\,dx=\frac{2(1-\cos n\pi)}{n\pi}.\end{aligned}$$ 当 $n$ 为偶数时 $b_n=0$；当 $n=2k-1$ 时 $b_n=\frac4{(2k-1)\pi}$。因此 $$f(x)\sim\frac4\pi\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{\sin(2k-1)x}{2k-1}.$$ 在 $x=0$ 处右端为 $0$，恰等于 $\frac{f(0^-)+f(0^+)}{2}=\frac{-1+1}{2}$，与狄利克雷定理一致。

部分和 $S_N(x)=\frac4\pi\sum_{k=1}^{N}\frac{\sin(2k-1)x}{2k-1}$ 在跳跃点附近并不单调逼近方波，而是出现吉布斯现象：在 $x=0$ 右侧，$S_N$ 的最大值超过 $1$，且当 $N\to\infty$ 时过冲量趋于跳跃高度 $2$ 的约 $9\%$（约 $0.18$）。增加项数只会使过冲区间变窄，不会使过冲幅度消失。原因是 $S_N$ 连续而极限函数在 $0$ 处间断，收敛在跳跃点附近不可能一致；过冲正是这种非一致收敛的定量表现，也说明傅里叶级数在间断点只能收敛到左右极限的平均值。

帕塞瓦尔等式把函数的总能量分解到各频率：若 $f$ 在 $[-\pi,\pi]$ 上平方可积，则 $$\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f^2(x)\,dx=\frac{a_0^2}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(a_n^2+b_n^2).$$ 对上面的方波，$f^2=1$，左边为 $\frac1\pi\cdot2\pi=2$，右边为 $\frac{16}{\pi^2}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(2k-1)^2}$，故 $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(2k-1)^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{8}$。再由 $$\begin{aligned}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{n^2}&=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(2k-1)^2}\\&\quad+\frac14\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{n^2},\end{aligned}$$ 解得 $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{n^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{6}$。这说明傅里叶系数不仅描述函数，还编码了它的能量分布。
en: Let $f$ be $2\pi$-periodic and integrable on $[-\pi,\pi]$. The trigonometric system $$1,\ \cos x,\ \sin x,\ \cos2x,\ \sin2x,\ \dots$$ is orthogonal: for $n,m\ge1$, $$\begin{aligned}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\cos nx\cos mx\,dx&=\pi\delta_{nm},\\ \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\sin nx\sin mx\,dx&=\pi\delta_{nm},\end{aligned}$$ $$\begin{aligned}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\cos nx\sin mx\,dx&=0,\\ \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\cos nx\,dx&=\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\sin nx\,dx=0.\end{aligned}$$ These identities follow directly from the product-to-sum formulas. Orthogonality is the reason the coefficients of each frequency can be isolated.

Suppose $f$ has a uniformly convergent trigonometric expansion $$f(x)=\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(a_n\cos nx+b_n\sin nx).$$ Multiply by $\cos kx$ ($k\ge1$) and integrate over $[-\pi,\pi]$. Uniform convergence permits termwise integration, and orthogonality makes every term except $a_k\cos kx$ integrate to $0$, so $$\begin{aligned}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\cos kx\,dx&=a_k\pi,\\ a_k&=\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\cos kx\,dx.\end{aligned}$$ Multiplying by $\sin kx$ similarly gives $b_k$. For $k=0$, $\int f=\frac{a_0}{2}\cdot2\pi=\pi a_0$, so $a_0=\frac1\pi\int f$; writing the constant term as $\frac{a_0}{2}$ makes the formula for $a_0$ uniform with the others.

Convergence is guaranteed by Dirichlet's theorem: if $f$ is $2\pi$-periodic, bounded and piecewise monotone (or piecewise smooth) on $[-\pi,\pi]$, with only finitely many discontinuities, then its Fourier series converges at every point, with sum $$S(x)=\frac{f(x^-)+f(x^+)}{2},$$ where $f(x^\pm)$ are the one-sided limits; at a continuity point $S(x)=f(x)$, and at a jump it is the average of the one-sided limits. At the endpoints $x=\pm\pi$ the sum is $\frac{f(-\pi^+)+f(\pi^-)}{2}$. Note that continuity alone does not guarantee convergence of the Fourier series (there are continuous functions whose Fourier series diverges at some point), so the piecewise monotonicity or piecewise smoothness hypothesis cannot be omitted.

Compute the square wave: let $f(x)=-1$ for $-\pi<x<0$, $f(x)=1$ for $0<x<\pi$, extended $2\pi$-periodically. Since $f$ is odd, $a_0=a_n=0$. For $n\ge1$, $$\begin{aligned}b_n&=\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)\sin nx\,dx\\&=\frac2\pi\int_0^{\pi}\sin nx\,dx=\frac{2(1-\cos n\pi)}{n\pi}.\end{aligned}$$ Thus $b_n=0$ for even $n$, while for $n=2k-1$, $b_n=\frac4{(2k-1)\pi}$. Therefore $$f(x)\sim\frac4\pi\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{\sin(2k-1)x}{2k-1}.$$ At $x=0$ the right-hand side is $0$, exactly $\frac{f(0^-)+f(0^+)}{2}=\frac{-1+1}{2}$, in agreement with Dirichlet's theorem.

The partial sums $S_N(x)=\frac4\pi\sum_{k=1}^{N}\frac{\sin(2k-1)x}{2k-1}$ do not approach the square wave monotonically near a jump; instead the Gibbs phenomenon appears. To the right of $x=0$, the maximum of $S_N$ exceeds $1$, and as $N\to\infty$ the overshoot approaches about $9\%$ of the jump height $2$ (about $0.18$). Adding more terms only narrows the region of overshoot; it never removes the overshoot itself. The reason is that $S_N$ is continuous while the limit function is discontinuous at $0$, so convergence near the jump cannot be uniform; the overshoot is a quantitative manifestation of this non-uniform convergence, and the series can only sum to the average of the one-sided limits at a jump.

Parseval's identity decomposes the total energy of the function across frequencies: if $f$ is square-integrable on $[-\pi,\pi]$, then $$\frac1\pi\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f^2(x)\,dx=\frac{a_0^2}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(a_n^2+b_n^2).$$ For the square wave above, $f^2=1$, so the left side is $\frac1\pi\cdot2\pi=2$, while the right side is $\frac{16}{\pi^2}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(2k-1)^2}$; hence $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(2k-1)^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{8}$. Since $$\begin{aligned}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{n^2}&=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac1{(2k-1)^2}\\&\quad+\frac14\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{n^2},\end{aligned}$$ we obtain $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac1{n^2}=\frac{\pi^2}{6}$. Fourier coefficients thus encode not only the function but also its energy distribution.

zh: 设 $u_n\ge0$，$S_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}u_k$。因为 $S_{n+1}-S_n=u_{n+1}\ge0$，部分和数列单调不减。由单调有界原理，$\{S_n\}$ 收敛当且仅当它有上界，即 $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}u_n\ \text{收敛}\iff\exists M>0,\ S_n\le M\ (\forall n).$$ 若部分和无上界，则 $S_n\to+\infty$，级数发散到 $+\infty$。改变有限项只把 $S_n$ 平移一个常数，不影响是否有界；因此判敛散性时只需看从某一项起的尾部。

比较判别法：若从某项起 $0\le u_n\le v_n$，则 $\sum v_n$ 收敛时，$\sum u_n$ 的部分和有上界，故 $\sum u_n$ 收敛；等价地，$\sum u_n$ 发散时 $\sum v_n$ 发散。极限形式更常用：设 $v_n>0$，$\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{u_n}{v_n}=l$。若 $0<l<+\infty$，则存在 $c,C>0$ 使 $cv_n\le u_n\le Cv_n$（充分靠后），两级数同敛散；若 $l=0$，则 $u_n\le v_n$（充分靠后），$\sum v_n$ 收敛可推出 $\sum u_n$ 收敛；若 $l=+\infty$，则 $u_n\ge v_n$（充分靠后），$\sum v_n$ 发散可推出 $\sum u_n$ 发散。参照级数通常取 $p$ 级数或几何级数。

比值判别法：设 $u_n>0$，$\rho=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{u_{n+1}}{u_n}$。若 $\rho<1$，取 $q$ 使 $\rho<q<1$，则充分靠后有 $\frac{u_{n+1}}{u_n}\le q$，从而 $u_n\le Cq^n$，与收敛的几何级数比较得 $\sum u_n$ 收敛。若 $\rho>1$，取 $q$ 使 $1<q<\rho$，则充分靠后 $u_{n+1}\ge qu_n$，故 $u_n\ge Cq^n\to+\infty$，通项不趋于 $0$，级数发散。若 $\rho=1$，判别法失效：$\sum\frac1n$ 与 $\sum\frac1{n^2}$ 的比值极限都等于 $1$，但前者发散、后者收敛。对一般项级数，把 $u_n$ 换成 $|u_n|$ 可判断绝对收敛；若 $\rho>1$，则 $|u_n|$ 不趋于 $0$，原级数也发散。

根值判别法：设 $u_n\ge0$，$\rho=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{u_n}$（若极限存在，$\rho$ 就是该极限）。若 $\rho<1$，取 $q$ 使 $\rho<q<1$，则充分靠后 $\sqrt[n]{u_n}\le q$，即 $u_n\le q^n$，故 $\sum u_n$ 收敛。若 $\rho>1$，取 $q$ 使 $1<q<\rho$，则有无穷多个 $n$ 满足 $\sqrt[n]{u_n}\ge q$，即 $u_n\ge q^n\ge1$，通项不趋于 $0$，级数发散。若 $\rho=1$，同样失效：$\sum\frac1n$ 与 $\sum\frac1{n^2}$ 的 $\rho$ 都等于 $1$。根值判别法对含 $n$ 次幂的通项最方便。

积分判别法：设 $f$ 在 $[1,+\infty)$ 上正、连续、单调递减，$u_n=f(n)$。对 $x\in[n,n+1]$ 有 $f(x)\le f(n)=u_n$，故 $\int_n^{n+1}f\le u_n$，求和得 $\int_1^{N+1}f\le S_N$；对 $x\in[n-1,n]$ 有 $f(x)\ge f(n)=u_n$，故 $u_n\le\int_{n-1}^{n}f$，求和得 $S_N-u_1\le\int_1^N f$。因此 $S_N$ 有界当且仅当 $\int_1^{+\infty}f$ 收敛。取 $f(x)=x^{-p}$：$p\ne1$ 时 $\int_1^{R}x^{-p}dx=\frac{R^{1-p}-1}{1-p}$，$p>1$ 时极限有限，$p<1$ 时趋于 $+\infty$；$p=1$ 时为 $\ln R\to+\infty$；$p\le0$ 时通项不趋于 $0$，直接发散。故 $\sum\frac1{n^p}$ 当且仅当 $p>1$ 时收敛。

综合例子：(1) $\sum\frac{n+1}{n^3+2}$，通项与 $\frac1{n^2}$ 同阶，取 $v_n=\frac1{n^2}$，则 $\frac{u_n}{v_n}=\frac{n^2(n+1)}{n^3+2}\to1$，由极限比较法收敛。(2) $\sum\frac{2^n}{n!}$，比值 $\frac{u_{n+1}}{u_n}=\frac2{n+1}\to0<1$，收敛。(3) $\sum\left(\frac{n}{2n+1}\right)^n$，根值 $\sqrt[n]{u_n}=\frac{n}{2n+1}\to\frac12<1$，收敛。策略是：先看通项是否趋于 $0$；含阶乘或连乘用比值，含 $n$ 次幂用根值，有理式用极限比较配 $p$ 级数；若 $\rho=1$，改用积分判别法或更精细的估计。
en: Let $u_n\ge0$ and $S_n=\sum_{k=1}^{n}u_k$. Since $S_{n+1}-S_n=u_{n+1}\ge0$, the partial sums are non-decreasing. By the monotone convergence principle, $\{S_n\}$ converges if and only if it is bounded above, i.e. $$\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}u_n\ \text{converges}\iff\exists M>0,\ S_n\le M\ (\forall n).$$ If the partial sums are unbounded, then $S_n\to+\infty$ and the series diverges to $+\infty$. Changing finitely many terms only shifts $S_n$ by a constant and does not affect boundedness; hence convergence depends only on the tail.

Comparison test: if $0\le u_n\le v_n$ eventually, then convergence of $\sum v_n$ bounds the partial sums of $\sum u_n$, so $\sum u_n$ converges; equivalently, divergence of $\sum u_n$ forces divergence of $\sum v_n$. The limit form is more practical: let $v_n>0$ and $\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{u_n}{v_n}=l$. If $0<l<+\infty$, then $cv_n\le u_n\le Cv_n$ eventually for some $c,C>0$, so the two series share the same behaviour; if $l=0$, then $u_n\le v_n$ eventually, so convergence of $\sum v_n$ implies convergence of $\sum u_n$; if $l=+\infty$, then $u_n\ge v_n$ eventually, so divergence of $\sum v_n$ implies divergence of $\sum u_n$. The reference series is usually a $p$-series or a geometric series.

Ratio test: let $u_n>0$ and $\rho=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{u_{n+1}}{u_n}$. If $\rho<1$, choose $q$ with $\rho<q<1$; eventually $\frac{u_{n+1}}{u_n}\le q$, hence $u_n\le Cq^n$, and comparison with a convergent geometric series gives convergence. If $\rho>1$, choose $q$ with $1<q<\rho$; eventually $u_{n+1}\ge qu_n$, so $u_n\ge Cq^n\to+\infty$, the terms do not tend to $0$, and the series diverges. If $\rho=1$ the test is inconclusive: $\sum\frac1n$ and $\sum\frac1{n^2}$ both have ratio limit $1$, yet the first diverges and the second converges. For a general series, apply the test to $|u_n|$ to detect absolute convergence; if $\rho>1$, then $|u_n|$ does not tend to $0$ and the original series diverges.

Root test: let $u_n\ge0$ and $\rho=\limsup_{n\to\infty}\sqrt[n]{u_n}$ (if the limit exists, $\rho$ is that limit). If $\rho<1$, choose $q$ with $\rho<q<1$; eventually $\sqrt[n]{u_n}\le q$, i.e. $u_n\le q^n$, so $\sum u_n$ converges. If $\rho>1$, choose $q$ with $1<q<\rho$; then $\sqrt[n]{u_n}\ge q$ for infinitely many $n$, so $u_n\ge q^n\ge1$ for those $n$, the terms do not tend to $0$, and the series diverges. If $\rho=1$ the test is again inconclusive: both $\sum\frac1n$ and $\sum\frac1{n^2}$ have $\rho=1$. The root test is especially convenient for terms containing $n$-th powers.

Integral test: let $f$ be positive, continuous and decreasing on $[1,+\infty)$, and let $u_n=f(n)$. For $x\in[n,n+1]$, $f(x)\le f(n)=u_n$, so $\int_n^{n+1}f\le u_n$; summing gives $\int_1^{N+1}f\le S_N$. For $x\in[n-1,n]$, $f(x)\ge f(n)=u_n$, so $u_n\le\int_{n-1}^{n}f$; summing gives $S_N-u_1\le\int_1^N f$. Hence $S_N$ is bounded if and only if $\int_1^{+\infty}f$ converges. Take $f(x)=x^{-p}$: for $p\ne1$, $\int_1^{R}x^{-p}dx=\frac{R^{1-p}-1}{1-p}$, which has a finite limit for $p>1$ and tends to $+\infty$ for $p<1$; for $p=1$ it is $\ln R\to+\infty$; for $p\le0$ the terms do not tend to $0$, so divergence is immediate. Therefore $\sum\frac1{n^p}$ converges exactly when $p>1$.

Combined examples: (1) For $\sum\frac{n+1}{n^3+2}$, the term has the same order as $\frac1{n^2}$; with $v_n=\frac1{n^2}$, $\frac{u_n}{v_n}=\frac{n^2(n+1)}{n^3+2}\to1$, so the series converges by the limit comparison test. (2) For $\sum\frac{2^n}{n!}$, the ratio is $\frac{u_{n+1}}{u_n}=\frac2{n+1}\to0<1$, so it converges. (3) For $\sum\left(\frac{n}{2n+1}\right)^n$, the root is $\sqrt[n]{u_n}=\frac{n}{2n+1}\to\frac12<1$, so it converges. Strategy: first check whether the terms tend to $0$; use the ratio test for factorials or products, the root test for $n$-th powers, and limit comparison with a $p$-series for rational expressions; if $\rho=1$, switch to the integral test or a sharper estimate.
